subject: Post-call recap: prioritized pain mapping & 30-day pilot proposal — Emberline Analytics
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Park <samantha.park@emberline.com>, Kenji Mori <kenji.mori@emberline.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: prioritized pain mapping & 30-day pilot proposal — Emberline Analytics

Hi Samantha / Kenji — thanks again for a productive discovery this morning. Quick recap and what we propose next so everyone has the same view.

Key pain points you emphasized:
- Inaccurate classification of short-form customer support logs (FPR high on short tickets) — major source of manual triage.
- Token cost spikes when running nightly batch scoring across 3MM rows (current setup is exceeding cost targets).
- No lightweight way to A/B model variants for routing without impacting latency SLAs.

Top goals for a successful 30-day engagement:
1) Improve classification precision on sub-50-token support snippets by at least 8-10% (primary metric: precision@threshold).
2) Demonstrate a >25% reduction in per-request token cost using batching + prefix cache with equivalent latency profile (secondary metric: cost per 10k requests).
3) Deliver a repeatable eval suite (10k prompt set) and an owners-playbook for rolling model variants into prod.

Proposed 30-day rapid pilot (outline):
- Week 0 (this week): Access & onboarding — data mapping template, short sample export (10k rows), IAM user for read-only S3 access or secure upload.
- Week 1: Baseline evals against current model; create prioritized prompt set focusing on short tickets.
- Week 2: Run inference experiments (batching, quantized model variant) in a dedicated sandbox.
- Week 3: Compare precision/cost tradeoffs, run controlled A/B for latency impact.
- Week 4: Compile findings, production handoff checklist, and evaluation artifacts for your MLOps.

Owners:
- Redwood AE: Dylan Brooks (pilot coordination, commercial)
- Redwood Solutions: Marissa Cole (onboarding, eval harness)
- Redwood Infra: Aditya Rao (sandbox infra + security checks)
- Emberline: Samantha Park (data & product owner), Kenji Mori (platform/infra)

Access asks (needed by Wed 08/25):
1) Small sample export (10k rows) with label column + schema notes (use the attached template).
2) Short-term S3 read-only creds OR secure upload link; if upload, please name folder EMB-30D-PILOT.
3) SOC2/IP/any relevant security evidence you can share — we'll provide the redwood stub template for minimal items.

Attachments: redwood_30d-pilot-charter.pdf (attached charter), emberline_data_mapping_template.xlsx

Next steps (agreed on call):
- Samantha: confirm sample availability and preferred transfer method by Wed EOD.
- Kenji: confirm whether Emberline will accept a temporary service account or prefers upload.
- Redwood: we'll provision the sandbox and send a short onboarding checklist by Tue.

Happy to iterate—if anything here doesn't match your view, call it out and I'll update.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[d] 415-555-0192

From: Samantha Park <samantha.park@emberline.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Kenji Mori <kenji.mori@emberline.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: prioritized pain mapping & 30-day pilot proposal — Emberline Analytics

Dylan — this is perfect, appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- We can produce the 10k sample by Thu 08/26; it will include the label column and a minimal PII redaction (we'll leave raw ids).
- For the sandbox transfer: Kenji prefers an upload to an SFTP location (security policy) rather than provisioning cloud creds. He can share the SFTP URL by EOD Tue.
- Security: we can share SOC2 summary and a short vendor assessment form — we'll attach to a reply. Full evidence may take longer but summary is fine for the pilot.

Two priorities for Emberline during the pilot: 1) don't regress latency for the live web route (90th percentile SLA is 250ms), and 2) keep evaluation artifacts reproducible so our ML infra team can iterate.

We'll confirm SFTP details and sample availability tomorrow. Thanks!

—Samantha
Samantha Park
Senior Product Manager, Emberline Analytics
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Park <samantha.park@emberline.com>, Kenji Mori <kenji.mori@emberline.com>

Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: prioritized pain mapping & 30-day pilot proposal — Emberline Analytics

Thanks Samantha — SFTP is fine. Two quick operational notes from our side:
- If SFTP, please include a short README with file names and schema defs so Marissa can map columns quickly.
- We'll ensure the sandbox routes traffic to a shadow environment only (no live traffic changes). Marissa: can you draft the eval harness plan this week and include the reproducibility checklist?

Kenji / Samantha — if EOD Tue is tight, Wed morning still works for us; we aim to kick the baseline runs by Fri.

I'll attach the charter and an empty report template to make results easy to consume.

Dylan
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 08:39:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: prioritized pain mapping & 30-day pilot proposal — Emberline Analytics

Adding a quick operational checklist for clarity — I'm putting together the eval harness and will share the prompt set tomorrow:
- I/O mapping: use emberline_data_mapping_template.xlsx (attached) — highlight which column is "short_ticket_text" and which is the label.
- Prompt set: 10k prompts with stratified sampling across short (<50 tokens) and long tickets; will deliver 3 stratifications: severity, product area, and ticket length.
- Baseline scripts: we'll run the baseline on your current model checkpoints (please confirm which model/dev branch if Emberline wants exact parity).
- Success gating: primary gate is precision lift on short tickets (>=8%); secondary gate is cost per 10k requests <= your target.
- Deliverables: weekly checkpoints Friday; final readout doc + runbook week 4.

I'll upload the initial prompt set to the shared doc and tag Kenji for infra notes.

—Marissa
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2027 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: prioritized pain mapping & 30-day pilot proposal — Emberline Analytics

Kenji / Samantha — quick checklist from infra/security to speed onboarding:
1) SFTP details (host, path, username, fingerprint) and confirmation we can download files from our temporary infra IP range 52.33.14.0/24. If you cannot whitelist an IP range, we'll follow the upload flow you prefer.
2) Minimum data requirements: CSV UTF-8, header row, columns: ticket_id, short_ticket_text, label, timestamp, product_area.
3) If there is PII beyond identifiers, let us know — we'll redact client-side if required.
4) Please attach the SOC2 summary or vendor questionnaire — the stub we sent shows the minimal items we need.

I'll provision the sandbox once SFTP is available and will share SSH jump details for the Redwood ops user. Expect a short onboarding packet from me within 24 hours of data being available.

Thanks — looking forward to getting baseline results.

Aditya Rao
Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
